summary: Both blocking defects are genuinely fixed, not relabelled. Kill provenance is a real, single-point variable whose removal or mis-hoisting is caught by mutation testing and confirmed by live probe; the mapping to PROCESS_UNKNOWN/MAIN_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE is the spec's own row for an outer kill without a retained terminal observation. No invented scalar survives in the matrix input, and PROCESS_SUCCESS is structurally unreachable from a caller that runs no collector, stop or timer — the spec-correct outcome, with the pure matrix still able to report success on observed facts. All seven added tests are load-bearing: each dies when the fix it guards is reverted. No pre-existing test was weakened; the two corrected expectations move toward the spec. F4 and F7 are de-scoped and honestly recorded, including a retraction of round one's overstatement. The residue is label coarseness inside an already-correct PROCESS_UNKNOWN/3 outcome plus a process-level gap in what abandonment means, all recorded as new low findings.

writeControlRecord is type-checked (:143) and awaited unconditionally (:147) with no try/catch; a throw propagates before runPrepared, so no child, listener or timer exists and nothing can hang or leak. Both rewritten tests assert rejection and an event log that stops at ['clock','write'] — stronger than what they replaced and consistent with spec lines 77 and 115. Mutating the swallow back fails both. See N5: that await is itself unbounded.

The promise always settles: probed with a successful kill and no close, a throwing kill and no close, a late close after the settle (no double settle, no unhandled rejection) and a close just before the deadline (zero kills). clearTimers() runs on all four settlement paths and clears both timers. The if(settled) check inside the deadline callback sits after the kill, which is the wrong order in principle but unreachable because settle and clearTimers are synchronous with close. See N3 for the process-level residue.

newFindings.title: every clean run reports a terminal write failure that never happened
newFindings.detail: With terminalEvidencePersisted unconditionally false, EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED is the outcome for every run that is not a known main failure or an unknown exit — including a zero exit with a valid schema-checked durable result — although no terminal write was attempted. Because :31 precedes :34 it also masks a real deadline crossing (kill denied, child then exits zero yields EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED rather than DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; measured). The closed vocabulary has no 'terminal evidence not attempted' code. Status and exit code stay the honest PROCESS_UNKNOWN/3, so this is a labelling defect, not a manufactured outcome.

newFindings.title: the new matrix row absorbs more specific failure codes for unknown exits
newFindings.detail: Exhaustive comparison over 368,640 inputs against a copy with the row removed: 4,608 classifications change, all with rawExit.kind==='unknown'. Two change status, PROCESS_SUCCESS/0 to PROCESS_UNKNOWN/3/MAIN_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE, closing a real hole in which success was reachable with no observed main exit. The other 4,606 keep PROCESS_UNKNOWN/3 but replace EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED (2,304), STOP_FAILED (1,920), STOP_RECEIPT_FAILED (192), DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (96), PARENT_LOST (48), CONTAINMENT_UNRESOLVED (24), TIMER_CANCEL_FAILED (20) and RESULT_WRITE_FAILED (2) with the less specific code. No input with exit, signal or null raw exit changed, so the insertion is precedence-safe for existing rows; the report's 'no change to existing ordering' is literally true but reads as a stronger claim than the code supports. No test pins the new row against those competing gates.

newFindings.title: abandonment settles the promise but does not release the child
newFindings.detail: After the abandonment bound fires, nothing destroys or unrefs child.stdout/child.stderr, no listener is removed, no escalation or second kill is attempted, and the result exposes no pid or process group. Measured with a real spawn: the promise settled at 305 ms while the parent process stayed alive 4,028 ms until the abandoned child exited, with diagnostics still accumulating (1 MiB cap) for no consumer. The bound is therefore on the promise, not on the caller's liveness, and the 'cleanup owner' the spec's deadline row requires retained cannot be read out of the result.

newFindings.title: asserted-but-unobserved boolean positions remain, and one lost its disclosure
newFindings.detail: startupValid:true, with startupWriteFailed, evidencePreexists, invocationIdMismatch, parentLost and resultWriteFailed at false, are positions this caller never observed — it starts no transient unit and reads no startup identity. They cannot promote a result or manufacture a terminal failure; their whole influence is on which PROCESS_UNKNOWN code is reported. Round one's report disclosed startupValid; the replacing report, which supersedes it in full, does not. Carry the disclosure forward.

newFindings.title: the mandatory control-record write is awaited without a bound
newFindings.detail: The durable read is wrapped in beforeDeadline(+1000 ms) at :89, but the control-record write is awaited with no deadline, and F5's fix puts that unbounded await on the only path to spawn. A hanging persistence worker therefore hangs the executor before any child exists — the hazard spec line 47 names explicitly. Pre-spawn, so no owned resource is at risk; low.

newFindings.title: the F3 containment validation no longer gates the disposition
newFindings.detail: containmentComplete reaches fault-matrix.mjs:35 only past :31, which this caller can never pass, so the new schema and status validation affects only diagnostics.resultReadFailed. The new F3 test asserts that flag and stays load-bearing, but the pre-existing test 'durable completion without independently observed containment remains unknown' now yields the same EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED for containment true and false and no longer tests its own title. CONTAINMENT_UNRESOLVED is unreachable from this caller (still reachable and tested in the pure matrix).

newFindings.title: the provenance downgrade is broader than the spec requires
newFindings.detail: killRequested suppresses every post-kill observation, including a genuinely retained exit/nonzero that merely coincided with the deadline (measured: exit 3 after a successful kill classifies as MAIN_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE). Spec line 68 constrains the signal row; absorbing a nonzero exit code as well is conservative over-application. The direction is safe — ownership retained rather than a financial failure decided — and the real observation survives in result.rawExit.

newFindings.title: validated options are re-read at spawn time, after an await boundary
newFindings.detail: args and env are read inside runPrepared, after the await on writeControlRecord that follows validation, so an injected writer could mutate either between check and use; env is additionally passed by reference rather than copied. Requires a hostile injected dependency, which is outside the module's trust model, but freezing or copying at validation time would close it. Related nit: the if(settled) guard in the deadline callback sits after killGroup rather than before it; unreachable in practice because settle and clearTimers are synchronous with close, but the safe order is the reverse.

descopingAssessment: Honest. F4 and F7 are stated as not attempted, in their own sections and again under explicit open work, and the report retracts round one's claim that the handoff requirement was implemented — the exact overstatement that made F4 a finding. The seven denial cases are named as unexercised. Absence independently confirmed. The unreachability of PROCESS_SUCCESS is also stated plainly and listed as unresolved future work rather than presented as completeness.
recommendedFollowUp: Add a matrix code (or a distinct field) for 'terminal evidence never attempted' so a clean run is not reported as EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED and a real deadline crossing is not masked (N1).
Decide the MAIN_EXIT_UNAVAILABLE row's placement deliberately against STOP_FAILED and DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, and pin it with a precedence test (N2).
Complete abandonment at the process level: destroy or unref the child pipes, remove listeners, and return the pid/process group so the outstanding cleanup owner is retained (N3).
Carry round one's startupValid disclosure forward into the current implementation record (N4).
Bound the control-record write the way the durable read is bounded (N5).
